purpose.statement: The ITDR server agent monitors Active Directory users and computer activities; session tracking can be enabled in the server agent policy to monitor logon activities, and password analysis to identify compromised or weak passwords by checking hashes against leaked databases, common patterns and custom dictionaries while monitoring for password reuse or rotation.

quotes: The Zscaler ITDR server agent monitors Active Directory (AD) users and computer activities
You can enable session tracking in the server agent policy to monitor logon activities.

You can also enable password analysis to identify compromised or weak passwords by checking hashes against leaked databases, common patterns, and custom dictionaries while also monitoring for password reuse or rotation.

settings-tabs.statement: Server Agent Settings (Settings > Server Agent Settings) has Domains, Agents, Agent Update Groups and Configuration tabs.

quotes: On the Server Agent Settings Page (Settings > Server Agent Settings), you can see the following tabs:
On the Domains tab, you can do the following:
On the Agents tab, you can do the following:
On the Agent Update Groups tab, you can do the following:
On the Configuration tab, you can do the following:

domains-table.statement: The Domains tab lists each domain with Total DCs (domain controllers assigned), Active, Inactive, Not Installed (domain controllers without a server agent) and Capabilities Installed.

quotes: Total DCs: The total number of domain controllers assigned to the domain.
Active: The number of active domain controllers.
Inactive: The number of inactive domain controllers.
Not Installed: The number of domain controllers that don't have a server agent installed.
Capabilities Installed: The capabilities installed on the domain controllers.

agents-table.statement: The server Agents table lists System Name, Domain Name, First Seen, Last Seen, OS Version, Version, Server Type (the type of AD server), DC Type (the type of domain controller) and IP.

quotes: System Name: The name of the system on which a server agent is installed.
Domain Name: The name of the domain.
First Seen: The date and time when the server agent was installed.
Last Seen: The date and time when the server agent was last connected to the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
Server Type: The type of AD server.
DC Type: The type of domain controller.
IP: The IP address of the system.
OS Version: The operating system (OS) name and version.
Version: The server agent's version number.

show-all-agents.statement: On the server Agents tab, Show all agents shows inactive server agents along with active ones when enabled and is disabled by default.

quotes: If enabled, inactive server agents are shown along with active agents.
By default, Show all agents is disabled.

agent-actions.statement: The Agents tab actions include Uninstall All Agents, Uninstall Selected, Delete Selected and Trigger Logs (fetching the activity log data used for troubleshooting), and an error log icon is available for critical events.

quotes: Uninstall All Agents: Uninstalls all server agents.
Uninstall Selected: Uninstalls only the selected server agents.
Delete Selected: Deletes the selected server agents.
Trigger Logs: Fetches the server agent activity log data used for troubleshooting, and makes it available to download.
Error logs are generated for critical events. Click the View Error Logs icon to view the error logs.

configuration-keywords.statement: The Configuration tab takes password keywords, up to 100 entries typed in, with a text file upload required for more than 100 entries.

quotes: You can enter up to 100 entries. If you want to enter more than 100 entries, you must upload a text file.
Enter password keywords of your choice.

update-groups-table.statement: The server Agent Update Groups tab enables phased updates, adds groups, and lists each group's Name, Selection Criterion, Update Progress (the total number of server agents updated in the group) and Update Enabled (checkmark for enabled, X for disabled).

quotes: Update Progress: The total number of server agents updated in the group.
The checkmark icon indicates that the updates are enabled for the group, and the X icon indicates that the updates are disabled for the group.
Name: The name of the server agent update group.
Selection Criterion: The selection criterion specified for the server agent update group.
Enable phased updates for the server agent update groups.
Add a server agent update group.
Update Enabled: The status of phased updates.

session-tracking.statement: Session tracking monitors logon activities for privileged accounts in the domain, and once enabled its details are viewed on the AD User Details page.

quotes: Session tracking is used to monitor logon activities for privileged accounts in the domain.
Session tracking is enabled, and you can view the details on the AD User Details page.

password-analysis.statement: Password analysis is enabled per domain with Enabled, an Agent chosen from the drop-down menu and a scan Frequency of Weekly, Monthly or Quarterly, and its details are shown in the Password Analysis dashboard.

quotes: Password analysis is used to identify compromised or weak passwords.
Agent: Select a server agent from the drop-down menu.
Frequency: Select a scan frequency (Weekly, Monthly, or Quarterly) from the drop-down menu.
Password analysis is enabled, and you can view the details in the Password Analysis dashboard.
Enabled: Select to activate password analysis.

remediation-enable.statement: Running remediations for risky AD identities through a server agent requires remediation to be enabled on the server agent domain, and only one server agent can be selected to run the remediation action.

quotes: To run remediations, you must enable remediation on the server agent domain.
Only one server agent can be selected to run the remediation action.
The remediation feature enables you to run remediations for risky Active Directory (AD) identities using a server agent.

threat-detection-context.statement: Server-agent threat detection enriches an attacker and target user with group memberships, Entra role assignments, basic info, AD and Entra posture checks, credential exposures, password analysis results and past threat detections.

quotes: Group memberships: The list of AD groups the user is part of.
Entra role assignments: The list of role assignments for the user in the Entra ID.
Basic info: Username, User Principal Name (UPN), Password Last Set, Organizational Unit (OU), Title, Department, etc.
AD Entra posture checks: The list of AD and Entra posture checks that the user is present in.
Credex user info: The list of credential exposures that the user is present in.
Password analysis: The results of the user's password analysis.
User past threat detections: The list of the user's past threat detections.

Zscaler ITDR identifies these threats and enriches the data with contextual information to make it easier to investigate and take required action. The following contexts are available for an attacker and target user:

threat-detection-options-a.statement: The domain Threat Detection dialog offers Enable All, Brute Force, Malicious Dpapi Usage, Suspicious Group Additions, Suspected Kerberoasting, Suspected Kerberoasting (Encryption Downgrade) and Suspected Asrep Roasting options.

quotes: Enable All: Detect all attacks.
Brute Force: Detect brute force attacks.
Malicious Dpapi Usage: Detect malicious export of Data Protection API (DPAPI) domain backup key.
Suspicious Group Additions: Detect suspicious group membership additions.
Suspected Kerberoasting: Detect Kerberoasting attacks.
Suspected Kerberoasting (Encryption Downgrade): Detect Kerberoasting via encryption downgrade.
Suspected Asrep Roasting: Detect AS-REP roasting attacks.

threat-detection-options-b.statement: The domain Threat Detection dialog also offers Suspicious Adminsdholder Modification, Suspected Dcsync, Suspected Dcshadow, Account Reconnaissance, Password Spray, External IP Authentication (DC) and Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly options.

quotes: Suspicious Adminsdholder Modification: Detect Admin Security Descriptor Holder (AdminSDholder) modifications.
Suspected Dcsync: Detect DCSync attacks.
Suspected Dcshadow: Detect DCShadow attacks.
Account Reconnaissance: Detect account reconnaissance attacks.
Password Spray: Detect password spray attacks.
External IP Authentication (DC): Detect login attempts from public IP addresses for credential theft, brute force attacks, or reconnaissance targeting exposed DCs.
Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly: Detect anomalous Kerberos ticket requests.

kerberos-ticket-baseline.statement: Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly detection requires identifying abnormal events by first establishing a baseline of normal behavior for two weeks.

quotes: Kerberos Service Ticket Anomaly: Detect anomalous Kerberos ticket requests. This requires identifying abnormal events by first establishing a baseline of normal behavior for two weeks.

registration-token.statement: The server agent registration token registers a domain controller with the ITDR Admin Portal during installation, after which a session key is generated for subsequent requests; regenerating the token means the old token can no longer install a server agent, so any automated installation should be stopped first.

quotes: An agent registration token is a unique key used to register a domain controller with the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal while installing the server agent.
After the agent is registered, a session key is generated and used for making subsequent requests with the ITDR Admin Portal.
If you regenerate the token, you cannot use the old token to install the server agent. Make sure to stop any automated installation before generating a new token.

download-installer.statement: Server agents are installed on domain controllers; Download Agent offers Windows (EXE) and Windows (MSI) installation types and downloads the latest version.

quotes: Server agents are installed on domain controllers and continuously monitor Active Directory activity for identity threat detection.
Windows (EXE)
Windows (MSI)
The latest version of the server agent is downloaded to your system.

export-config.statement: Server agent configuration can be exported as CSV or JSON for all agents or filtered agents, filtered by system, OS version, server agent version or IP address; two export options export only the agents shown in the table, which displays only the active server agents, and Show All Agents in the Actions menu is the option to include inactive agents.

quotes: You can export server agent configuration details as a CSV or JSON file.
the server agents filtered by the system on which it is installed, the OS version of the system, the server agent version, or the IP address of the server
The table displays only the active server agents.
If you want to export all agents including the inactive agents, enable the Show All Agents option from the Actions drop-down menu.
These two options allow you to export only the agents that are shown in the table.

agent-logs.statement: After Actions > Trigger Logs on a server agent, a Download icon appears under the Actions column after 15 minutes, and the logs download as a compressed .zip file.

quotes: After 15 minutes, a Download icon appears under the Actions column of the selected server agent.
The server agent logs are downloaded to your local system in a compressed (.zip) file.
Click Actions > Trigger Logs.

uninstall.statement: Server agents can be uninstalled individually, selected, or all at once; the server agent tries to remove policies from the servers for three days before uninstalling itself.

quotes: You can uninstall a single agent, multiple agents, or all server agents from the ITDR Admin Portal.
The server agent tries to remove the policies from the servers for three days, and then it uninstalls itself.

delete.statement: Deleting a server agent removes its entry from the ITDR Admin Portal only and does not uninstall the agent, and server agents cannot be deleted if their Last Seen value is under 7 days.

quotes: When you delete a server agent, its entry is removed from the ITDR Admin Portal only. The agent is not uninstalled from the server.
Server agents cannot be deleted if their Last Seen value is under 7 days.

install-prerequisites.statement: Domain controllers for a server agent need Windows Server 2012 R2 or later (active or Read-only Domain Controller), .NET Framework 4.8 or later, 4 GB free memory, 500 MB disk space (5 GB for Password Analysis), 256 Kbps bandwidth (1 Mbps for Password Analysis), and HTTPS port 443 connectivity to ib.smokescreen.io and the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

quotes: Operating System: Windows Server 2012 R2 or later with an active Domain Controller or a Read-only Domain Controller
.NET Framework version 4.8 or later
Free memory: 4 GB
Disk space: 500 MB (5 GB for Password Analysis)
Internet bandwidth: 256 Kbps (1 Mbps for Password Analysis)
Connectivity over HTTPS (port 443) to the following domains:
ib.smokescreen.io
Zscaler Deception Admin Portal

install-parameters.statement: The server agent installer parameters are /qn (silent mode, required), /CMC=<instance name> (hostname of the ITDR Admin Portal, required), /REGKEY=<Registration Token> (required) and /PROXIES=<Proxy String> (optional, comma-separated with no white spaces).

quotes: | /qn | Enables silent mode installation | Yes |
| /CMC=<instance name> | The hostname of the ITDR Admin Portal | Yes |
| /REGKEY=<Registration Token> | The Server Agent Registration Token | Yes |

| /PROXIES=<Proxy String> | Proxies to connect to the ITDR Admin Portal. If there is more than one proxy, separate them with a comma. Make sure that there are no white spaces in the PROXIES parameter. | No |

proxy-order.statement: The server agent tries the PROXIES list left to right; if all fail it tries the SYSTEM user's proxy and then a direct no-proxy connection; credentials with special characters must be URL-encoded.

quotes: When the server agent starts, it attempts to connect to the ITDR Admin Portal using the list of proxies in a sequence from left to right.
If all of the above methods fail, the agent attempts to connect to the ITDR Admin Portal using the SYSTEM users proxy. If this also fails, the agent attempts a direct no-proxy connection.
If the username and password have special characters (e.g., Username = user#2211 and password = pass@123), you must URL-encode them.

proxy-pac.statement: To use a PAC file the server agent is directed to a URL where the PAC file is hosted, in the form http://<ip/host>/<pacfile>.pac.

quotes: To configure a proxy to use a PAC file, you must direct the server agent to a URL where the PAC file is hosted.
http://<ip/host>/<pacfile>.pac

update-group-criteria.statement: A server agent update group selects by Hostname List (exact match) or Hostname RegEx, and Zscaler recommends an enabled catch-all "All systems" group with .* after testing so all servers are upgraded.

quotes: Hostname List: Applies updates to all the agents where the hostname of the system exactly matches the hostnames specified in the Hostname List field.
Hostname RegEx: Applies updates to all the agents where the hostname of the system matches the hostname pattern specified as a regular expression in the Hostname RegEx field.
Zscaler recommends that you add a group named "All systems" with a catch-all regular expression ( .* ), and enable this group after you complete the testing to make sure all servers are upgraded.

phased-updates.statement: Phased updates are enabled or disabled with the Enable Phased Updates and Disable Phased Updates buttons, and enabling stops any automatic updates for agents that are not part of the groups.

quotes: Click Enable Phased Updates to enable the phased updates, or click Disable Phased Updates to disable.
Enabling this feature stops any automatic updates for agents that are not a part of the groups.

update-group-icons.statement: On the server Agent Update Groups page, the page says to click the checkmark icon under the Actions column to disable phased updates for a group and the X icon to enable them.

quotes: Under the Actions column, click the checkmark icon to disable phased updates for an agent update group, or click the X icon to enable phased updates.

additional-agents.summary: The what-is page lists as a benefit that ITDR works with Client Connector without additional agents or VMs; the server agent page says server agents are installed on domain controllers.

quotes: Integrates with Zscaler Client Connector to unlock new capabilities and protection without the need for additional agents or virtual machines (VMs).

positions.says: ITDR integrates with Zscaler Client Connector to unlock new capabilities without the need for additional agents or virtual machines.

quotes: Server agents are installed on domain controllers and continuously monitor Active Directory activity for identity threat detection.

positions.says: Server agents are installed on domain controllers and continuously monitor Active Directory activity for identity threat detection.

additional-agents.impact: The pages do not say whether the server agent counts as an additional agent beyond Client Connector, so an answer about what must be installed names both.

inactive-definition.title: When a server agent counts as inactive
inactive-definition.detail: The server Agents tab has Show all agents, disabled by default, but no captured server-agent page states when a server agent becomes inactive; the endpoint Agents page defines inactive as a last check-in older than 7 days.

password-analysis-agent.title: What the Agent selection for password analysis changes, and why it needs 5 GB and 1 Mbps
password-analysis-agent.detail: The page has the Agent drop-down and the Password Analysis disk and bandwidth figures but states neither the load the chosen agent carries nor the basis of the figures.

remediation-actions.title: Which AD remediation actions the server agent runs
remediation-actions.detail: The Managing Domains page says remediation runs risky AD identity remediations through one selected server agent but does not list the actions; the captured release notes name them with a date.

egress-hosts.title: What each egress host in the server agent prerequisites carries
egress-hosts.detail: The prerequisites name ib.smokescreen.io and the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal for HTTPS on port 443 without saying what each carries.

update-icon-result.title: What the Update Enabled icon shows after a click on the server update groups page
update-icon-result.detail: The Managing page's instruction and the About page's table give opposite meanings to the checkmark and X icons for the same column; neither says what the icon shows after the click.
